title: Story 01: New Feature Request — Full Lifecycle
pmResponse:
# Complete Action Plan: "Add search functionality to the issue list"

## Overview

A new feature request arrives for search functionality. This spans both sub-teams: the Library team builds the search API, then the Webapp team builds the search UI against the released library. I'll create a parent issue, break it down into 7 worker tasks (following the correct phase flow per sub-team) plus 1 sync tracker, wire up blockages for the dependency chain, and set the parent to `in-progress`.

---

## Issue Hierarchy (Visual Tree)

```
[Parent]  "Add search functionality to the issue list"
          tags: feature, initiative  |  assignee: project-manager  |  status: in-progress
          priority: 2
          │
          ├── [Child 1] "Design search API for issue list"
          │   tags: task, feature  |  assignee: library-architect  |  status: todo
          │   Phase: Library — Plan
          │
          ├── [Child 2] "Implement search functionality in library"
          │   tags: task, feature  |  assignee: library-developer  |  status: todo
          │   Phase: Library — Dev  |  BLOCKED BY: Child 1
          │
          ├── [Child 3] "Validate search functionality in library"
          │   tags: task, feature  |  assignee: library-validator  |  status: todo
          │   Phase: Library — Validate  |  BLOCKED BY: Child 2
          │
          ├── [Child 4] "Release library with search functionality"
          │   tags: task, feature  |  assignee: library-releaser  |  status: todo
          │   Phase: Library — Release  |  BLOCKED BY: Child 3
          │
          ├── [Child 5] "Implement search UI in webapp"
          │   tags: task, feature  |  assignee: webapp-developer  |  status: todo
          │   Phase: Webapp — Plan+Dev  |  BLOCKED BY: Child 4
          │
          ├── [Child 6] "Style search UI components"
          │   tags: task, feature  |  assignee: webapp-styler  |  status: todo
          │   Phase: Webapp — Style  |  BLOCKED BY: Child 5
          │
          ├── [Child 7] "Validate search UI in webapp"
          │   tags: task, feature  |  assignee: webapp-validator  |  status: todo
          │   Phase: Webapp — Validate  |  BLOCKED BY: Child 6
          │
          └── [Child 8] "Sync: Search feature complete"
              tags: sync  |  assignee: project-manager  |  status: todo
              BLOCKED BY: Child 7
```

---

## Detailed Command Sequence

### Phase A: Create Parent Issue

**Command 1 — Create the parent feature initiative:**
```bash
agt create "Add search functionality to the issue list" \
  --description "Feature request: Add search and filter functionality to the issue list. Users should be able to find issues by text query, status, tags, and other criteria. This feature spans both the Library sub-team (search API) and the Webapp sub-team (search UI). Breakdown covers: Library Plan → Library Dev → Library Validate → Library Release → Webapp Dev → Webapp Style → Webapp Validate." \
  --tags feature,initiative \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2
```
> **Reasoning:** Creates the top-level container for all work. Uses `feature,initiative` tags to signal this is a multi-phase feature effort. Assigned to PM as the accountable owner. Priority 2 (normal). Status starts as `todo` — will be moved to `in-progress` after all children are created.

→ Capture returned ID as `$PARENT_ID`

---

### Phase B: Create Worker Child Issues (Library Sub-team)

**Command 2 — Library Plan (library-architect):**
```bash
agt create "Design search API for issue list" \
  --description "Design the search/filter API for the issue list in the library. Define search parameters (text query, status, tags, assignee), query syntax, return types, pagination, and integration points. Consider the webapp's UI needs — the webapp will need to display search results, provide filter controls, and show search metadata. Produce a clear API spec that the library-developer can implement and the webapp-developer can integrate against." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee library-architect \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2 \
  --parentId $PARENT_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** First task in the pipeline. The library-architect designs the architecture and produces a spec. No blockers — this starts immediately. Tagged `task,feature` to indicate it's a feature task. Description explicitly calls out cross-team coordination needs.

→ Capture returned ID as `$CHILD1_ID`

**Command 3 — Library Dev (library-developer):**
```bash
agt create "Implement search functionality in library" \
  --description "Implement the search/filter functionality in the library based on the architecture spec produced by the library-architect. Build the search API endpoints, query parsing, filtering logic, and result formatting. Ensure the implementation is performant for large issue lists and matches the spec exactly. Update any relevant type definitions." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee library-developer \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2 \
  --parentId $PARENT_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** Second task — the library-developer codes the search feature from the spec. Blocked by the planning task (blockage added later). Description references the spec so the developer knows where to find requirements.

→ Capture returned ID as `$CHILD2_ID`

**Command 4 — Library Validate (library-validator):**
```bash
agt create "Validate search functionality in library" \
  --description "Write comprehensive tests for the new search functionality. Cover: text search queries, filter combinations (status, tags, assignee), edge cases (empty results, special characters, very long queries), pagination, performance with large datasets, and API contract correctness. Report any bugs as new issues and block this task until they are resolved." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee library-validator \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2 \
  --parentId $PARENT_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** Validation phase — the library-validator writes tests and checks quality. Blocked by library-dev. Description is specific about what to validate so the validator has clear acceptance criteria.

→ Capture returned ID as `$CHILD3_ID`

**Command 5 — Library Release (library-releaser):**
```bash
agt create "Release library with search functionality" \
  --description "Prepare and publish the library release containing the new search functionality. Steps: run the full test suite (all tests must pass), generate API documentation for the search endpoints, bump the version number, build the package, and publish to npm. Verify the published package can be installed and the search API works correctly." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee library-releaser \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2 \
  --parentId $PARENT_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** Release phase — the library-releaser packages and publishes. Blocked by library-validate. This is the final gate before the webapp team can integrate.

→ Capture returned ID as `$CHILD4_ID`

---

### Phase C: Create Worker Child Issues (Webapp Sub-team)

**Command 6 — Webapp Dev (webapp-developer):**
```bash
agt create "Implement search UI in webapp" \
  --description "Implement the search UI for the issue list in the webapp. This covers planning and development: design the search interaction, build the search input component, add filter controls (by status, tags, assignee), integrate with the library's released search API, and display search results with proper loading/empty states. The library must be released before starting this task — use the published npm package." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee webapp-developer \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2 \
  --parentId $PARENT_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** The webapp-developer handles planning + development for the webapp. Blocked by library release (Child 4) because the webapp needs the actual released library package to integrate properly. This prevents API mismatches and rework. The description notes this dependency explicitly.

→ Capture returned ID as `$CHILD5_ID`

**Command 7 — Webapp Style (webapp-styler):**
```bash
agt create "Style search UI components" \
  --description "Apply visual polish to the search UI components built by the webapp-developer. Ensure: consistent styling with the rest of the application, responsive design across screen sizes, proper visual feedback for active filters, hover/focus states on search inputs, and smooth transitions for result loading. Do NOT change functionality — visual polish only." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee webapp-styler \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2 \
  --parentId $PARENT_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** Styling phase — webapp-styler polishes after the developer builds the feature. Blocked by webapp-dev. Description explicitly scopes the work to visual-only changes.

→ Capture returned ID as `$CHILD6_ID`

**Command 8 — Webapp Validate (webapp-validator):**
```bash
agt create "Validate search UI in webapp" \
  --description "Test the search UI end-to-end. Verify: search queries return correct results, filters combine correctly, UI is responsive after styling, loading and empty states display properly, keyboard navigation works, and integration with the library search API is solid. Run E2E tests covering key search workflows. Report any bugs as new issues." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee webapp-validator \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2 \
  --parentId $PARENT_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** Final validation — webapp-validator tests the complete feature including styled UI and library integration. Blocked by webapp-style. This is the last worker task before the sync tracker fires.

→ Capture returned ID as `$CHILD7_ID`

---

### Phase D: Create Sync Tracker

**Command 9 — Sync tracker (project-manager):**
```bash
agt create "Sync: Search feature complete" \
  --description "Sync tracker for the 'Add search functionality to the issue list' feature. This issue is blocked by the last worker child (webapp validation). Once unblocked, the PM reviews all child issues for completion, verifies quality, updates the parent status, and reports to stakeholders." \
  --tags sync \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2 \
  --parentId $PARENT_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** This is the sync tracker — a sentinel issue assigned to the PM that fires when all worker tasks are done. When this becomes unblocked, the PM knows the full pipeline has completed and can close out the feature. Tagged `sync` to distinguish it from work tasks.

→ Capture returned ID as `$CHILD8_ID`

---

### Phase E: Wire Up Blockages (Dependency Chain)

The dependency chain follows the phase flows exactly:

**Command 10 — Library Dev blocked by Library Plan:**
```bash
agt blockages add $CHILD2_ID --by $CHILD1_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** Library development cannot start until the architecture spec is complete.

**Command 11 — Library Validate blocked by Library Dev:**
```bash
agt blockages add $CHILD3_ID --by $CHILD2_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** Testing cannot start until the implementation exists.

**Command 12 — Library Release blocked by Library Validate:**
```bash
agt blockages add $CHILD4_ID --by $CHILD3_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** Cannot release until validation confirms quality.

**Command 13 — Webapp Dev blocked by Library Release:**
```bash
agt blockages add $CHILD5_ID --by $CHILD4_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** The webapp needs the released library package to integrate. This is the critical cross-team handoff point. Blocking on release (not just plan or validate) ensures the webapp integrates against a stable, tested, published API.

**Command 14 — Webapp Style blocked by Webapp Dev:**
```bash
agt blockages add $CHILD6_ID --by $CHILD5_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** Styling must happen after the feature is functionally built.

**Command 15 — Webapp Validate blocked by Webapp Style:**
```bash
agt blockages add $CHILD7_ID --by $CHILD6_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** Final validation tests the complete, polished feature.

**Command 16 — Sync Tracker blocked by Webapp Validate:**
```bash
agt blockages add $CHILD8_ID --by $CHILD7_ID
```
> **Reasoning:** The sync tracker fires when the last worker task completes. This is the PM's signal that the full pipeline has finished.

---

### Phase F: Add Context Comments

**Command 17 — Comment on parent issue:**
```bash
agt comments add $PARENT_ID --content "Feature breakdown complete. 8 child issues created covering the full lifecycle:

LIBRARY PIPELINE (Plan → Dev → Validate → Release):
  1. Design search API (library-architect)
  2. Implement search functionality (library-developer)
  3. Validate search functionality (library-validator)
  4. Release library with search (library-releaser)

WEBAPP PIPELINE (Dev → Style → Validate):
  5. Implement search UI (webapp-developer)
  6. Style search UI (webapp-styler)
  7. Validate search UI (webapp-validator)

SYNC TRACKER:
  8. Sync: Search feature complete (project-manager)

Dependency chain: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 7 → 8
Critical handoff: Library Release (4) → Webapp Dev (5)
Parent set to in-progress. Workers will drive their own transitions. PM will be notified via sync tracker (#8) when all work is complete."
```
> **Reasoning:** Documents the full breakdown, dependency chain, and process for anyone viewing the parent issue. Serves as the single source of truth for the feature's structure.

**Command 18 — Comment on first worker task (library-architect):**
```bash
agt comments add $CHILD1_ID --content "You are the first task in this feature pipeline. Please design the search API with these webapp needs in mind: search input (text query), filter by status/tags/assignee, paginated results, and result metadata. Your spec will be the foundation for all subsequent work across both teams. When complete, update this issue to 'todo' and assign back to project-manager for reassignment to library-developer."
```
> **Reasoning:** Gives the architect specific requirements and context about downstream consumers. Explains the handoff protocol.

**Command 19 — Comment on sync tracker:**
```bash
agt comments add $CHILD8_ID --content "Sync tracker — this issue will become unblocked when the webapp validation (Child 7) is complete. At that point: (1) review all child issues for completion, (2) verify no open bugs remain, (3) update the parent issue status to 'done', (4) report feature completion to stakeholders."
```
> **Reasoning:** Documents the PM's post-completion checklist so the PM knows exactly what to do when the sync tracker fires.

**Command 20 — Comment on the cross-team handoff task (webapp-developer):**
```bash
agt comments add $CHILD5_ID --content "Cross-team handoff: You are blocked by the library release (Child 4). Once unblocked, install the newly published library package and integrate the search API into the webapp. Plan the search UI interaction yourself (planning is part of your role), then implement the search input, filters, and result display. Your work will be styled by the webapp-styler after you complete this task."
```
> **Reasoning:** The webapp-developer task is the critical handoff point between teams. This comment makes the dependency explicit and gives guidance on what to do.

---

### Phase G: Activate the Pipeline

**Command 21 — Set parent to in-progress:**
```bash
agt update $PARENT_ID --status in-progress
```
> **Reasoning:** Moves the parent to `in-progress` to signal that work has begun. This prevents the work loop from re-waking the PM every cycle. The PM now waits for the sync tracker (Child 8) to fire.

**Command 22 — Add status comment on parent:**
```bash
agt comments add $PARENT_ID --content "Status: IN PROGRESS. Pipeline activated. Library architect (Child 1) is unblocked and can start immediately. All other tasks are blocked by their upstream dependencies. PM is waiting on sync tracker (Child 8) for completion signal."
```
> **Reasoning:** Final status update documenting that the pipeline is live and the PM is in a waiting state.

---

## Dependency Chain Summary

```
Child 1 (Lib Plan) ──blocks──► Child 2 (Lib Dev)
Child 2 (Lib Dev)  ──blocks──► Child 3 (Lib Validate)
Child 3 (Lib Val)  ──blocks──► Child 4 (Lib Release)
Child 4 (Lib Rel)  ──blocks──► Child 5 (Web Dev)      ← cross-team handoff
Child 5 (Web Dev)  ──blocks──► Child 6 (Web Style)
Child 6 (Web Sty)  ──blocks──► Child 7 (Web Validate)
Child 7 (Web Val)  ──blocks──► Child 8 (Sync Tracker) ← PM re-engagement
```

---

## Key Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| **Webapp dev blocked by library release (not just plan)** | Safest approach — the webapp integrates against a stable, tested, published API. Prevents rework from API changes between plan and release. |
| **Linear chain, not parallel** | Library work must complete before webapp work begins. The search API is a hard dependency for the UI. No parallelism is possible across teams. |
| **Library follows 4-phase flow (Plan→Dev→Validate→Release)** | Standard feature flow for the Library sub-team. |
| **Webapp follows 3-phase flow (Dev→Style→Validate)** | Matches the Webapp sub-team's defined phase flow. Planning is bundled with development for webapp-developer. |
| **Sync tracker blocked by last worker (Child 7)** | Ensures PM re-engages only after ALL work is done, including final validation. |
| **Parent set to `in-progress`** | Prevents the work loop from re-waking PM. PM waits passively for the sync tracker. |
| **Comments on key handoff points** | Architect (first task), webapp-developer (cross-team handoff), and sync tracker (PM re-engagement) get extra context because they are the critical transition points. |

---

## Post-Pipeline: What Happens Next

Once workers drive the pipeline to completion:

1. **Workers drive their own transitions** — each worker marks their task done and triggers the next via blockage resolution.
2. **When Child 8 (sync) becomes unblocked** — PM wakes up, reviews all children, verifies quality, updates parent to `done`, and reports completion.
3. **If any worker finds a bug** — they create a new bug issue, which follows the bug flow: Reproduce → Dev → Validate → Release, potentially creating a side branch in the dependency tree.
feedback: Core structure is correct — parent feature with worker children + sync tracker, proper dependency chain, correct status transitions (todo → in-progress after children), and sync tracker assigned to PM blocked by last worker. However: (1) Agent expanded scope beyond expected output, adding 3 webapp children not in the spec (5→7) when only library-team work was expected; (2) Parent tagged 'feature,initiative' instead of just 'feature', children tagged 'task,feature' instead of just 'task', sync tracker missing 'task' tag; (3) Comment on Child 1 instructs architect to 'update to todo and assign back to PM for reassignment' — this contradicts the expected auto-blockage-resolution pattern where workers mark done and system resolves dependencies automatically. Assignment mapping and sync tracker pattern are strong.
